paper.title_en: RIFT for the O4 era: operating points, calibration marginalization, and cross-code validation
paper.abstract_en: The Rapid Iterative FiTting (RIFT) parameter inference algorithm provides a simulation-based-inference approach to efficient, highly-parallelized parameter inference for GW sources. In this paper, we describe improvements deployed during preparations for and analysis of O4 observations (versions 0.0.17.3--0.0.18.0) that broaden RIFT's reach for single-event inference with contemporary instruments. We provide additional options to increase compatibility and comparability with other codes, notably including (a) enhancing RIFT's capabilities for calibration marginalization; (b) managing our likelihood's internal, output, and time-interpolated representation; (c) introducing new coordinates for (transverse) spin and eccentric mean anomaly, enabling more robust inference of parameters with subtle and complex correlations to others, and (d) revised operating point choices better suited to the loudest, clearest signals. We identify and reconcile the most substantial sources of head-to-head likelihood differences between RIFT and other production inference codes, and describe automated waveform symmetry checks that detect upstream model regressions before they bias inference. Using the previously-reported RIFT/asimov interface for reproducible settings consistent with past work, we demonstrate these capabilities end to end.
